parole.significato: aluminum (chemical element, a light, silvery metal, with atomic number 13)
parole.testo: From English alumina (“aluminum oxide”), from Latin alumen (“alum, bitter salt”). The name of this metal in English, aluminum, was created from alumina in 1812 by Sir Humphrey David.

From English bowl, probably via German Bowle. Alternative historical forms: bols. First attested use to mean a bowl for making punch – 1880. First attested use to refer to the beverage itself – 1886.

parole.significato: a baby, an infant or a toddler
parole.testo: From English baby. Alternative historical forms: bebijs, bēbijs. First attested use – 1911.
From English designer.

parole.significato: dollar (name of the monetary units of several countries, includgin the United States, Canada, and Australia)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English dollar, from early Dutch daler, daalder, from German Taler, Thaler (“dollar”), from Sankt Joachimsthaler, coins from the Saint Joachim valley (German Tal means "valley").

parole.significato: durian (any of several trees of genus Durio; their fruit)
parole.testo: From English durian, from Malay durian, from Proto-Malayic *duri-an, from (Western) Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *duʀi-an.

parole.significato: file (aggregation of data on a storage device)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English file.

parole.significato: folklore (tales, legends and other oral tradition items of a given population or ethnic group)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English folklore, itself a compound of folk and lore, imitating German terms like Volkslehre (“people's customs, ethnology”).

parole.testo: Via other European languages, ultimately borrowed from English international (apparently coined in 1780 by Jeremy Bentham from Latin inter (“between”) and New Latin nationalis), adapted to follow Latvian patterns ( + -āls).

parole.significato: (male) calculator, computer (a man whose work it is to perform mathematical calculations and computations)
parole.testo: A borrowing from other European languages, possibly originally English calculator.

parole.significato: cue (long stick with a pointy end used in certain games, especially pool or billiards)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English cue.

parole.significato: queer (not confirming to conventional sexual or gender norms)

parole.significato: radon (gaseous chemical element, with atomic number 86.)

parole.significato: loudspeaker (electromechanical device that converts an electric signal into audible sound)
parole.testo: From skaļš (“loud”) + runa (“talk”), made into a second declension masculine noun (ending -is). Calque of English loudspeaker.

parole.significato: a Scot or Scotsman, a man from Scotland
parole.testo: From English Scot, from Latin Scōtī, Scōttī, itself of unknown, presumably Celtic, origin.
